questions.title: Safe Quotient Guard
questions.description:
A math worksheet generator divides numbers that students type, and a zero denominator must not crash it.
Read two integers, print their integer quotient, and guard the division with try/except ZeroDivisionError.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer a
Line 2: integer b

Output Format:
Print a // b, or the exact line: Cannot divide by zero

Constraints:
0 <= a <= 1000, 0 <= b <= 1000

questions.title: Cast Rescue Integer
questions.description:
A data-entry tool converts typed values to integers, but operators sometimes mistype.
Read one line, convert it with int() inside try/except ValueError, and report either the number or the failure.

Input Format:
One line: the raw value

Output Format:
The integer if the conversion succeeds, otherwise exactly: Not a number

Constraints:
Line length 1..20

questions.title: Index Rescue Lookup
questions.description:
A lookup tool prints the item at a requested position of a number list, guarding against bad positions.
Read the list, then the index, and print the item - catching IndexError for out-of-range positions.

Input Format:
Line 1: space-separated integers
Line 2: the index k

Output Format:
The number at index k, or exactly: Index out of range

Constraints:
1 <= len(nums) <= 20, 0 <= k <= 10

questions.title: Missing Key Patrol
questions.description:
A stockroom service maps item codes to shelf labels and must respond politely to unknown codes.
Read n key-value pairs, then a query key; print its value, catching KeyError for missing keys.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: key value (single words)
Last line: the query key

Output Format:
The stored value, or exactly: Key not found

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10, keys and values are single words
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 10, keys and values are single words

questions.title: Audit Trail Order Demo
questions.description:
A billing script demonstrates that a finally block runs after the main work, whatever happens.
Read an integer n, print n * 2 inside a try block, and print the audit line from a finally clause.

Input Format:
One line: integer n

Output Format:
Line 1: n * 2
Line 2: Audit done

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
try:
    print(n * 2)
finally:
    print("Audit done")

questions.title: Negative Amount Rejector
questions.description:
A ledger clerk rejects negative amounts by raising a ValueError with a message and catching it to print the message.
Read an integer amount; if it is negative, raise ValueError("Negative amount") and catch it to print the message; otherwise confirm acceptance.

Input Format:
One line: integer amount

Output Format:
Either exactly: Negative amount
Or: Accepted <amount>

Constraints:
-1000 <= amount <= 1000

questions.title: Cab Fare Split Desk
questions.description:
Friends split a weekend cab fare equally, and the desk app must survive a buggy entry of zero heads.
Read the fare and the number of heads; print each share using integer division inside try/except ZeroDivisionError with the exact error line.

Input Format:
Line 1: fare (integer)
Line 2: heads (integer)

Output Format:
Either: Each pays: <fare // heads>
Or exactly: Heads cannot be zero

Constraints:
0 <= fare <= 100000, 0 <= heads <= 50

questions.title: ATM Cashout Safety Gate
questions.description:
An ATM refuses withdrawals larger than the balance by raising ValueError("Insufficient funds") and catching it to print the message.
Read the balance and the requested amount.

Input Format:
Line 1: balance (integer)
Line 2: amount (integer)

Output Format:
Either: Dispensed <amount>
Or exactly: Insufficient funds

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 100000, 0 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Robust Age Parser
questions.description:
A hospital kiosk asks visitors to type their age; sometimes the screen gets junk.
Read the typed line, convert it with int() inside try/except ValueError, and answer politely.

Input Format:
One line: the typed age value

Output Format:
Either: Age: <value>
Or exactly: Invalid age

Constraints:
Line length 1..10

questions.title: Attendance Batch Parser
questions.description:
A school office scans register entries one per line; smudged lines are not numbers.
Parse each line in its own try/except ValueError, collect the line numbers that failed, and report them numbered, followed by the counts.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of entries
Next n lines: each entry (a valid integer or garbage)

Output Format:
First, one line per bad entry, in order: Line <i>: invalid entry
Then: Valid entries: <count>
Then: Invalid entries: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, each line length 1..20
questions.sampleoutput1:
Line 2: invalid entry
Line 4: invalid entry
Valid entries: 3
Invalid entries: 2
questions.output1:
Line 1: invalid entry
Line 3: invalid entry
Valid entries: 2
Invalid entries: 2
questions.output2:
Line 1: invalid entry
Valid entries: 0
Invalid entries: 1
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
errors = []
valid = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    line = input()
    try:
        int(line)
        valid += 1
    except ValueError:
        errors.append(i)
for i in errors:
    print(f"Line {i}: invalid entry")
print(f"Valid entries: {valid}")
print(f"Invalid entries: {len(errors)}")

questions.title: Data Repair Bench
questions.description:
A data-repair macro replays saved operations; some crash, and the bench must print a verdict per operation. ValueError and ZeroDivisionError are caught by their own specific clauses, and everything else falls through to the generic handler that names the exception type.
Operations (tokens separated by single spaces):
- SUM a b: print int(a) + int(b)
- DIV a b: print int(a) // int(b)
- PICK i: print boxes[int(i)] where boxes = ["crate", "pallet", "bin"]
- LOOK key: print rates[key] where rates = {"bolt": 5, "nut": 2}
Verdicts: a ValueError prints BAD NUMBER; a ZeroDivisionError prints DIV BY ZERO; the generic except Exception handler prints GENERIC <TypeName> using type(e).__name__.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: one operation each

Output Format:
One verdict line per operation, in order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, PICK index 0..10, SUM/DIV arguments are integer strings or garbage
questions.input1:
4
SUM x 1
DIV 8 2
PICK 0
LOOK washer
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 20, PICK index 0..10, SUM/DIV args are integer strings or garbage

questions.title: Grade Sheet Commit
questions.description:
A university upload tool commits a bonus-marks update only when the new total stays within the 100-mark cap; otherwise it rolls back.
Either way, the finally clause prints the audit line last.

Input Format:
Line 1: current total (integer)
Line 2: bonus marks (integer)

Output Format:
If total + bonus <= 100: COMMIT <bonus> then AUDIT total=<new total>
Otherwise: ROLLBACK <bonus> then AUDIT total=<unchanged total>

Constraints:
0 <= total <= 100, 0 <= bonus <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
total = int(input())
bonus = int(input())
new_total = total
try:
    if total + bonus > 100:
        raise ValueError("over cap")
    new_total = total + bonus
    print("COMMIT", bonus)
except ValueError:
    print("ROLLBACK", bonus)
finally:
    print(f"AUDIT total={new_total}")

questions.description:

Next n lines: item qty (item is a single word, qty an integer)

Output Format:
Per successful add: Added <item> x<qty>
On the first overflow: Cart is full
Finally: Items in cart: <count>

questions.title: Ticket Escalation Chain
questions.description:
A helpdesk routes critical tickets upward: the routing step logs the ticket and then re-raises the alert so the outer handler prints the escalation line.
For each ticket: if the severity is critical, print LOG <id> from the inner handler, re-raise with a bare raise, and let the outer handler print ESCALATED: <message> where the message is: Ticket <id> needs a human. Non-critical tickets print OK <id>.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: ticket_id severity (severity is one of: low, major, minor, critical)

Output Format:
One or two lines per ticket, in order: OK <id>, or LOG <id> followed by ESCALATED: Ticket <id> needs a human

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, ids 1..10 chars, severity in low, major, minor, critical

T2 critical
T3 low

questions.title: Form Validator Three Errors
questions.description:
A signup pipeline validates every field of every applicant and never stops at the first problem.
Define three custom exception classes: BlankFieldError, BadFormatError and OutOfRangeError (all subclass Exception), raise them from a validator function, and catch each with its own except clause.
Rules per field: a field submitted as a single hyphen - is blank (BlankFieldError). The email field must contain both @ and . (otherwise BadFormatError). The age field must be a digit string (otherwise BadFormatError) whose value is between 1 and 120 inclusive (otherwise OutOfRangeError). The name field has no extra rule beyond blankness.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of applicants
Per applicant, 3 lines: name, email, age

Output Format:
Per field, in order: <field>: OK or <field>: <ExceptionName>
Per applicant: Valid fields: <good>/3
Finally: Applicants fully valid: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5, each field line 1..40 chars, a lone hyphen marks blank

questions.title: Reactor Shutdown Sequence
questions.description:
A reactor console runs a comma-separated step list inside a nested try/finally: every step has a cleanup guarantee, a failure aborts the rest, and the reactor is always released.
Steps BOOT, SCAN and VENT print run <step> then cleanup <step>; FAIL raises RuntimeError("step FAIL exploded"). The inner finally prints cleanup <step> even for a failing step. The outer handler prints abort: <message> and skips the remaining steps, and the outer finally prints release reactor. When every step succeeds the console prints all steps complete before releasing.

Input Format:
One line: comma-separated steps from BOOT, SCAN, VENT, FAIL

Output Format:
The deterministic console transcript, one line per event.

Constraints:
1 <= steps <= 10, steps from BOOT, SCAN, VENT, FAIL
questions.sampleoutput1:
acquire reactor
run BOOT
cleanup BOOT
run SCAN
cleanup SCAN
run VENT
cleanup VENT
all steps complete
release reactor
questions.sampleoutput2:
acquire reactor
run BOOT
cleanup BOOT
cleanup FAIL
abort: step FAIL exploded
release reactor
questions.output1:
acquire reactor
cleanup FAIL
abort: step FAIL exploded
release reactor
questions.output2:
acquire reactor
run SCAN
cleanup SCAN
run SCAN
cleanup SCAN
run VENT
cleanup VENT
run BOOT
cleanup BOOT
all steps complete
release reactor
questions.output3:
acquire reactor
run VENT
cleanup VENT
cleanup FAIL
abort: step FAIL exploded
release reactor
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= steps <= 10, steps from BOOT, SCAN, VENT, FAIL

questions.title: Batch Settlement Engine
questions.description:
A payment switch replays a batch of stored operations; each operation is dispatched to a guarded runner and failures are collected instead of crashing the batch.
The switch catches everything with except Exception as e and records the exception's class name via type(e).__name__.
Operations: DIV a b (integer division int(a) // int(b)), PARSE s (int(s)), GET key (rate_table[key] with rate_table = {"plan1": 199, "plan2": 499}).

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: one operation each

Output Format:
Per successful operation, immediately: OK <line number> <value>
After all operations: Failed: <count>
Then one line per failure, in order: <line number> <ExceptionTypeName>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, GET key may be plan1, plan2 or unknown, DIV/PARSE args are integer strings or garbage
questions.input1:
3
PARSE abc
DIV 5 x
GET plan2
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 20, DIV/PARSE args are integer strings or garbage, GET key any single word
questions.blacklist: except ValueError, except KeyError, except ZeroDivisionError

questions.title: Gateway Charge Chainer
questions.description:
A payment gateway parses each transaction amount.
When the amount text is not an integer, the parser catches ValueError and raises a custom GatewayError chained with from, carrying the message DECLINED: bad amount <raw>. The outer loop catches only GatewayError and prints its message; valid amounts print CHARGED <amount>.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: one amount text per line (digit string or garbage)

Output Format:
Per transaction, in order: CHARGED <amount> or DECLINED: bad amount <raw>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, each line length 1..9
